techniques.name: Access Token Manipulation
techniques.description: Adversaries may modify access tokens to operate under a different security context, perform privilege escalation, or evade detection mechanisms.

techniques.name: Token Impersonation/Theft
techniques.description: Adversaries may duplicate or steal existing access tokens from running processes to impersonate logged-in users.

techniques.name: Create Process with Token
techniques.description: Adversaries may create new processes using stolen access tokens to execute binaries under high privilege accounts.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.description: Adversaries may disable or modify security tools such as EDR agents, antivirus, and firewall rules to avoid detection.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts to execute malicious payloads.

techniques.name: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse cmd.exe to execute commands on targeted Windows systems.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with malicious attachments to gain initial execution.

techniques.name: Dynamic-link Library Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries may inject dynamic-link libraries into process memory spaces to run code disguised as legitimate software.

techniques.name: Cloud Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries may compromise cloud accounts to maintain access, escalate privileges, and execute actions on cloud resources.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information on Mobile
techniques.description: Adversaries may compress or encrypt mobile application code to evade app store review and on-device detection.

techniques.name: Unauthorized Command Message
techniques.description: Adversaries may send unauthorized industrial protocol command messages to alter physical manufacturing equipment behavior.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Parent technique for Command and Scripting Interpreter.

groups.name: APT29
groups.description: Threat group attributed to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR).

groups.name: Lazarus Group
groups.description: North Korean state-sponsored cyber threat group.

groups.name: FIN7
groups.description: Financially motivated threat group operating out of Eastern Europe.

software.name: Mimikatz
software.description: Credential dumping tool capable of extracting plaintext passwords and Kerberos tickets.

software.name: Cobalt Strike
software.description: Commercial threat emulation software frequently leveraged by adversaries for C2 and post-exploitation.

campaigns.name: SolarWinds Supply Chain Compromise
campaigns.description: Global supply chain intrusion campaign targeting government and IT enterprise networks in 2020.

procedures.description: APT29 duplicated LSASS tokens to escalate privileges on compromised domain controllers.
Cobalt Strike Beacon executes PowerShell commands encoded in Base64 via powershell.exe -e.
Lazarus Group modified registry keys to disable Windows Defender real-time monitoring service.
Adversaries used stolen SAML token signing certificates to forge cloud access tokens across Azure AD.

mitigations.name: Privilege Account Management
mitigations.description: Restrict user account privileges and implement Just-In-Time (JIT) access policies.

mitigations.name: Disable or Restrict Feature or Program
mitigations.description: Disable PowerShell v2 and constrain PowerShell language modes to prevent execution of unverified scripts.

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.description: Ensure EDR driver files and service registry keys are read-only for system administrators.

detections.strategy: Monitor process creation and token impersonation API calls (e.g. ImpersonateLoggedOnUser, DuplicateTokenEx).
analytics: SIGMA Rule: Suspicious Process Creation via Stolen Token
YARA Rule: Token Stealing Shellcode In-Memory

detections.strategy: Monitor service stop signals and registry key changes under HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender.
analytics: SIGMA Rule: Windows Defender Realtime Protection Disabled

d3fendTechniques.name: Access Control Verification
d3fendTechniques.description: Verifying authorization tokens and scope boundaries before processing execution requests.

d3fendTechniques.name: Process Execution Analysis
d3fendTechniques.description: Analyzing command line arguments and child process trees for anomalous execution paths.

d3fendTechniques.name: Software Health Monitoring
d3fendTechniques.description: Monitoring security agent health and isolating endpoints when EDR protection is terminated.

d3fendTechniques.name: System Restore & Immutable Snapshot Recovery
d3fendTechniques.description: Restoring operating system state and critical volumes from immutable cloud or hardware snapshots.
